label: EU(7)-PIM: tramadol
title: Tramadol in an older person
statement: Tramadol, both sustained-release and standard (non-sustained-release) forms, is a medicine to avoid in older people. It causes more side effects in older adults, such as confusion, vertigo and nausea. Start with a low dose and go slowly. Over the age of 75, daily doses above 300 mg of the standard form are not advised. In severe renal failure, the 2015 list advised avoiding sustained-release tramadol. For immediate-release tramadol it suggested a lower dose and a longer interval between doses.

plain_summary: Tramadol is an opioid pain medicine. In people aged 65 and over it can cause confusion, dizziness and nausea, so a low dose and a review are advised.

medicine_groups.name: Tramadol, standard and sustained-release
medicine_groups.note: Tramacet and Zaldiar are tramadol with paracetamol. Generic packs that show the ingredient name with a company name count too. One group is used for the sustained-release and standard forms because the published limits differ only in the dose advice.

rule_for_models: Suspect a finding when tramadol (any brand, standard or sustained-release, alone or with paracetamol) is supplied to a person aged 65 or over. One supply is enough. If age is unknown and the supply otherwise qualifies, report only a possible finding and ask the pharmacist to confirm that the person is 65 or older. For a person over 75, mention a prescribed daily tramadol dose above 300 mg for the standard form or a sustained-release form. Calculate the tramadol component from strength and directions. For a person over 75, if the prescribed daily dose or maximum is unclear, keep the age-and-supply finding and ask the pharmacist: What daily dose or maximum did the prescriber specify for tramadol, in mg per day? Record the confirmed value or Not known. Record the amount the patient takes separately. For as-needed directions, report the prescribed maximum if known and distinguish it from the amount taken. When discussing the finding, ask how much tramadol the patient takes on a usual day and whether they have noticed confusion, dizziness or nausea.
cannot_be_seen: Why tramadol was prescribed, kidney function, and whether the person has side effects. Also how much is really taken and medicines supplied by a hospital or another pharmacy.
ask_the_gp: A review of whether tramadol is still needed and whether the dose is as low as possible.
